newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates ease in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates ease in liquid market.

text.p: * Central bank's dollar purchases injects liquidity

Philippine interbank call loan rates eased further on Friday to an average of 11.0125 from 12.03125 as the Central Bank's dollar purchases in the past three to four days put more cash in the system, traders said.
On Thursday too, rates had fallen and traders said the downtrend continued because demand for cash was low.
Being the last day for banks to meet weekly reserves, most had already met their requirements, they said.
One trader estimated the Central Bank had injected about 8.0 billion pesos in the past three or four days.
In the secondary market for treasury bills, rates on 91 day bills were a shade down. Standard Chartered Bank quoted its bid offer at 11.725/11.625 percent compared to 11.75/11.55 on Thursday.

Traders said they expected secondary market T bill rates to ease next week as the Bureau of Treasury was not holding its routine Monday auction in view of the holiday announced for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperaqtion (APEC) summit. This would mean money meant for T bills would remain uninvested.
Adding further to liquidity would be the maturity next week of T bills and and a floating rate note totally worth about 10 billion pesos, traders said.
